story.description: Build a reusable, authorable introductory content block for the homepage area titled DISNEY IMAGINATION CAMPUS - STUDENT TRAVEL REIMAGINED. The captured content includes a video area, playback helper text, the page theme heading, and two interactive calls to action: PLAY FULL VIDEO and LEARN MORE. Detailed typography, color values, pixel spacing, hover behavior, video source, poster image, transcript, and duration were not captured and must remain configurable rather than hardcoded.
accessibilityCriteria: The video interaction supports keyboard operation using Enter or Space, matching the captured playback instruction.
Both calls to action expose clear accessible names matching their visible labels: PLAY FULL VIDEO and LEARN MORE.

implementationAnalysis.rationale: The Content Agent document (finalAuthoringContract) contains a grounded 'Hero Video' block (componentId: component-001, canonicalBlockName: hero-video, selector: div.herovideo) sourced directly from https://www.disneycampus.com/. The live page confirms the block renders as div.herovideo with class 'block', height 438.75px at y:64 (immediately below the 64px header), full viewport width 780px. The authored table has a single data row with four cells: [video asset], [heading: DISNEY IMAGINATION CAMPUS - STUDENT TRAVEL REIMAGINED], [primary CTA link: PLAY FULL VIDEO], [secondary CTA link: LEARN MORE]. Section metadata for the containing section provides subtitles, poster, and transcript as configurable assets — these are NOT block cells but section-metadata rows and must be handled via the section-metadata block, not hardcoded. The block does not exist in the repository (inventory shows: cards, columns, footer, fragment, header, hero, widget — no herovideo). The canonical block name from the live site stylesheet is 'herovideo' (https://www.disneycampus.com/blocks/herovideo/herovideo.css is loaded), matching the div.herovideo selector. The story acceptance criteria require: exact text content rendered (Video label, playback helper text, heading, two CTAs), one configurable video media area, no hardcoded unavailable values, keyboard operation for video (Enter/Space), and accessible names on both CTAs. The block JS must: (1) read the four authored cells — video link/asset, heading, primary CTA, secondary CTA; (2) build a <video> element with keyboard play/pause via keydown Enter/Space; (3) expose aria-label on both CTA anchors matching their visible text; (4) render a visible 'Video' label and the playback helper text 'Press Enter or Space to play or pause the video.' as authored. The section-metadata (subtitles, poster, transcript) is already handled by the EDS section-metadata block and will be available as data attributes or section properties — the herovideo block JS should read poster and subtitles from the section's dataset if present, keeping them configurable. Typography (InspireTWDCBlack, font-weight:900, font-size:24px for CTAs; heading styles) and colors (white text on video overlay) are observed from computed styles but must not be hardcoded as magic values — they must use CSS custom properties scoped to the block. The PLAY FULL VIDEO link has aria-label 'PLAY FULL VIDEO about DISNEY IMAGINATION CAMPUS - STUDENT TRAVEL REIMAGINED' and href '#fullscreen-cta' in the live page; LEARN MORE has aria-label 'LEARN MORE about DISNEY IMAGINATION CAMPUS - STUDENT TRAVEL REIMAGINED' and href '/about'. These destinations are configurable per acceptance criteria. The block CSS must be mobile-first, use CSS custom properties for all visual tokens, and not hardcode pixel spacing or color values that were marked uncaptured.

filePlan.reason: New block decorator. Reads the four authored cells from the single table row: cell[0]=video asset (link or picture), cell[1]=heading text, cell[2]=primary CTA link (PLAY FULL VIDEO), cell[3]=secondary CTA link (LEARN MORE). Builds: a

New block stylesheet. Mobile-first layout: block is position:relative, full-width (width:100%), video fills the block as a background-like layer (position:absolute or object-fit:cover). Overlay content (label, helper text, heading, CTAs) positioned over the video. Uses CSS custom properties (--herovideo-text-color, --herovideo-cta-font-family, --herovideo-cta-font-size, --herovideo-cta-font-weight, --herovideo-heading-font-family) so values remain configurable and not hardcoded. CTA links styled as inline-flex buttons. Responsive breakpoint at 900px for desktop layout adjustments. No hardcoded color hex values or pixel dimensions for uncaptured properties.

assumptions: The canonical block folder name is 'herovideo' (matching div.herovideo selector and the loaded stylesheet URL https://www.disneycampus.com/blocks/herovideo/herovideo.css), not 'hero-video' (which is the canonicalBlockName in the contract). The EDS convention maps the CSS class directly to the folder name. The authored table header 'Hero Video' becomes class 'hero-video' via toClassName(), but the live site uses 'herovideo' without a hyphen. The implementation uses 'herovideo' to match the live site's actual block class and folder convention observed in the stylesheet URL.

The authored table row has exactly four cells per the Content Agent table structure: cell[0]=video asset (a link to the .mp4 or a picture element), cell[1]=heading (DISNEY IMAGINATION CAMPUS - STUDENT TRAVEL REIMAGINED), cell[2]=primary CTA link (PLAY FULL VIDEO with configurable href), cell[3]=secondary CTA link (LEARN MORE with configurable href). The JS decorator reads these four cells in order.

Section-metadata rows (subtitles, poster, transcript) are authored in the section-metadata block in the same section, not as cells in the herovideo block table. The herovideo JS reads these from the parent section's dataset after EDS processes section-metadata (e.g., section.dataset.subtitles, section.dataset.poster, section.dataset.transcript), or falls back gracefully if absent.

The 'Video' text node and 'Press Enter or Space to play or pause the video.' helper text are rendered by the block JS as constructed DOM elements (not authored as separate cells), since they appear as standard video accessibility affordances that the block decorator generates programmatically. This matches the live site pattern where these appear inside div.herovideo.

InspireTWDC font families are not available in the repository's fonts.css. The block CSS references them as CSS custom properties (--herovideo-cta-font-family, --herovideo-heading-font-family) with Arial/sans-serif fallbacks, so the block degrades gracefully in the boilerplate environment and can be overridden when the project fonts are added.

The PLAY FULL VIDEO CTA href '#fullscreen-cta' observed in the live page is a configurable destination per acceptance criteria AC5. The authored document will provide the actual href. The JS does not hardcode '#fullscreen-cta'.

The video element is rendered with muted and playsinline attributes by default (standard practice for autoplay-capable hero videos) but autoplay is not set, since the block's purpose is user-initiated playback via the keyboard/click interaction described in the acceptance criteria.
risks: MEDIUM: The authored table header 'Hero Video' produces class 'hero-video' via EDS toClassName(), but the live site block uses class 'herovideo' (no hyphen). If the Content Agent authors the block as 'Hero Video', EDS will generate div.hero-video, not div.herovideo. The implementation files must be placed at blocks/herovideo/ to match the live site convention, but the authored class will be hero-video. This mismatch requires either: (a) the Content Agent uses 'Herovideo' as the table header, or (b) the block folder is named hero-video. This is flagged as a content gap — the Content Agent should confirm the exact table header spelling to ensure the generated class matches the folder name.

LOW: Section-metadata dataset propagation timing — the herovideo block may decorate before section-metadata is processed by EDS, meaning section.dataset.poster etc. may not be available synchronously. The JS should read these values lazily or use a MutationObserver fallback, or read directly from the section-metadata block's DOM rows before they are removed.

LOW: The repository's fonts.css does not include InspireTWDC. The block will render with Arial fallback until the project's font assets and @font-face declarations are added. This is expected for a migration project and is not a blocker.

LOW: The video element's keyboard handler (Enter/Space) must not conflict with the browser's native video controls if controls attribute is present. The implementation should use controls-less video with a custom play/pause button or ensure the keydown handler is on a focusable wrapper element, not the video element itself, to avoid double-firing with native controls.
